data.notes:
Human Flow: Migration and Refugee Encampment (at CILAS). Shan Yang, Teaching Fellow, Cairo Institute of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Summer 2021 (preliminary syllabus).

This seminar examines people’s lifeworlds - on the move, in the transition, contained, encamped. It explores global mobilities, citizenship, division of labor and developmentalism through a critical lens.

Migrations do not just happen - they are produced. Capitalist modernity requires massive displacement that seamlessly supports the free flow of labor in the context of globalization. Yet mobile subjects are categorized, sorted and governed in and through the international legal order by initiatives dealing with trafficking, refugees, immigrant labor, sexual morality and border controls. The impact of these different initiatives on cross-border movements is mediated by gender, class, religion, sexual, and marital status.

As part of CILAS’s efforts to build social infrastructure for caring commons, this summer course attempts to open up the following possibilities:
- Participants from financially disadvantaged backgrounds are welcome to apply for course fee waiver and a subsidize for commute cost.
- CILAS will offer one “study day” each week for participants to use CILAS as a space to read, discuss and chill out.
- Tea and refreshments will be served during course meetings.

Course arrangements also include epigraphs quoting Pablo Neruda, a chant outside the Internment Center for Foreigners in Barcelona, Auden WH. 1962 (“Refugee Blues”) and Michael Hardt and Antonio Negri (Empire). They are not recorded as readings.

Session 4 lists the same Agier reading as Session 3. The Session 8 readings are marked as to be confirmed in the flow.
